intro: The restaurant pack: tables on a floor, menus with options, the kitchen's stations, recipes with what each dish costs, and tips kept apart from sales. Switch it on for the places that serve food in Settings › Industry packs; cafés, bars and counter service use it too.
start: Switch the restaurant pack on in Settings › Industry packs, for every place or only the places that serve food.
Check Restaurant rules: service charge, tips, split bills, voids and comps, and what short stock does.
Make your first menu and put dishes from the catalogue on it. Prices come from the price book.
Draw the floor with its tables, so the tills and the Floor screen show them.
Set up the kitchen, so each dish goes to the station that makes it.

articles.title: Draw the floor and its tables
articles.summary: Add your floors, such as inside or the terrace, then add tables and drag them where they stand.

steps.rest: on Draw the floor, give it a name and size, and press Add.
Give it a name, a shape and its seats, with the fewest it is laid for, and press Add.
or select it and move it with the arrow keys. Hold Shift for a bigger step.
Every table moved is saved together, and the tills see the new floor.

tips: A table with a party at it cannot be retired.
Tables never sit on top of each other: a move that would do that is refused and nothing moves.

articles.title: Send each dish to the right station
articles.summary: Stations are the places in the kitchen or bar that make dishes, each with its own screen. Rules say which station makes what.

steps.lead: Press Set up a kitchen and a bar

tips: A station set on the dish itself beats every rule. Then a rule for the dish beats one for its category, which beats one for its course.
A station used by a dish or a rule cannot be retired.

articles.title: Write a recipe and see what a dish earns
articles.summary: Say what one batch of a dish uses. Its ingredients leave stock when the kitchen starts it, and you see the cost of a portion and its margin.

steps.rest: on Recipes and dish costs, and find the dish.

The list shows the cost of a portion, the price, what it earns without tax and the margin.

tips: A dish with a recipe must not be counted in stock itself, or it would leave stock twice. Where the stock check warns about this, press Fix stock type.
An ingredient can have a recipe of its own, such as a sauce or a dough.
An ingredient never received has no cost, so the dish shows no margin until it has one.

articles.title: Mark a dish sold out
articles.summary: Say a dish has run out, and every till and menu at the place stops selling it until you bring it back.

tips: Restaurant rules can mark a dish sold out by itself when its ingredients cannot make another portion. It comes back when stock arrives.

articles.summary: A price rule changes the price book's price by time, day, date or kind of order, without keeping a second price list.

articles.title: Share out tips and pay them
articles.summary: Tips are never sales. Share a period's tips by a policy, approve the shares and pay them in cash or through payroll.
before: A tip policy for the place, and the people who take part on its roster.
